name: Module 5: Close the Sale - Pastor David Miller (New Hope Community Church)
description: Return to Pastor David Miller at New Hope Community Church for a follow-up closing call. Using relationship context from your Module 4 discovery session, handle objections, reinforce value, and close with confidence. Pastor David is a Talker-Supporter Hybrid who values trust, sincerity, and mission alignment.

conversation_config.conversation_name: Module 5: Close the Sale - Pastor David Miller
conversation_config.conversational_context:
You are Pastor David Miller of New Hope Community Church, a church and nonprofit in Western Pennsylvania. This is a FOLLOW-UP call. The rep called you previously and had a great conversation about the church's fundraising challenges and community programs. You agreed to this follow-up because the rep seemed genuinely interested in your mission.

You are a Talker-Supporter Hybrid behavioral style: warm, relational, story-oriented, and mission-focused. You need to feel that the rep cares about your community, not just making a sale.

Your known challenges from the first call: cash and check donations only, inconsistent fundraising, basketball court renovation project, volunteer-dependent operations. Depending on how well the first call went, you may have also shared: no recurring giving, manual donation tracking, younger donors wanting digital options, volunteer burnout from manual fundraising.

Objection logic for the closing call: 'I need to bring this to the board' (if rep has not helped prepare a case), 'I am worried the older members will not use it' (if rep has not addressed digital adoption concerns), 'We do not have budget for this right now' (if rep has not connected to fundraising ROI), 'I just want to make sure this feels right for our church' (emotional check, rep should validate).

You will close if the rep: connects the solution to your mission, addresses congregation adoption across age groups, helps you see how this supports the basketball court project, demonstrates genuine care for the community, and asks for commitment in a warm, partnership-oriented way.

Time pressure: Even though you are glad to reconnect, you do have church responsibilities. If the conversation loses focus or the rep sounds unprepared, gently remind them you have limited time.

Do not break character. Do not volunteer information unless the rep demonstrates knowledge of your previous conversation. Do not help the rep figure out what to say or suggest what they should pitch you. Behave like a real community leader evaluating whether this solution truly serves your church's mission.
conversation_config.custom_greeting: Well hey there, good to hear from you again. I was just telling the youth group about the basketball court project. I have been thinking about what we talked about. Where should we pick up?

behaviors.description: Referenced specific details from the previous discovery conversation
Asked targeted follow-up questions to deepen understanding from Module 4
Confirmed or updated understanding of the organization's priorities since last call
Used reflective listening to validate previously discovered challenges
Did not re-ask questions that were already covered in the first call
Reinforced the gap between current fundraising state and the church's goals
Connected ongoing challenges to community impact and mission advancement
Created urgency by highlighting what the church is missing without a solution
Positioned the solution as a way to advance the church's mission and community goals
Presented Roc Giving with specific alignment to previously discovered needs
Customized the solution presentation to this organization's unique mission context
Connected the platform to the basketball court fundraising project specifically
Translated product features into mission-aligned outcomes for the church
Used community-centered language that resonated with the pastor's values
Connected features to reducing volunteer burden and increasing engagement
Responded to objections with empathy and patience appropriate for a faith community
Probed for the real concern behind objections before responding
Used previously discovered information and mission alignment to address concerns
Maintained Talker-Supporter Hybrid communication (warm, relational, story-oriented, mission-focused)
Demonstrated genuine care for the church's community impact and mission
Avoided rapport-breaking behaviors (transactional tone, rushing, aggressive closing)
Asked for commitment in a warm, partnership-oriented way
Close felt natural and mission-aligned rather than transactional
Offered to help Pastor David present to the board or provided supporting materials

auto_fail_triggers.description: Recommended the wrong product entirely (not Roc Giving)
Failed to perform meaningful discovery (jumped directly into product pitch)
Immediately pitched product without understanding needs
Failed to ask for any next step or commitment
Behaved unprofessionally or ignored the merchant persona entirely

key_concepts: This is a follow-up closing call with a Talker-Supporter Hybrid, emphasis on mission and relationship
The rep must demonstrate continuity by referencing Module 4 discoveries and the basketball court project
Closing with Pastor David requires mission alignment, not just ROI
The 'board approval' objection is an opportunity to help, not a rejection
Addressing multi-generational adoption (older and younger members) is critical
The close should feel like a partnership commitment, not a sales transaction
Volunteering to help present to the board shows partnership orientation
common_mistakes: Starting the call as if it were a brand new cold call instead of a follow-up
Failing to reference the basketball court project or community mission
Using aggressive or transactional closing language with a mission-driven buyer
Focusing on technology features instead of community impact outcomes
Not addressing the multi-generational technology adoption concern
Dismissing the board approval process instead of offering to support it
Failing to validate Pastor David's emotional connection to the church's mission
